items.title: Pilot transfer operation: A safer step aboard
items.summary: Safe pilot transfer operations depend on both correct procedures and fit-for-purpose equipment. New SOLAS requirements entering into force in 2028 will introduce mandatory performance standards for pilot transfer arrangements, and some existing installations may require physical modifications. items.title: India introduces new requirements for ships in coastal waters
items.summary: Foreign ships calling at Indian ports, operating in Indian coastal waters or transiting those waters may fall within an expanded regulatory regime. A transition period applies to specified additional requirements until 1 April 2027.

items.title: New Fire Drill Guidelines for Vehicle Carrying Vessels
items.summary: The Vehicle Carrier Safety Forum (VCSF) has published Fire Drill Guidelines for Vehicle Carrying Vessels, providing operators with a structured framework for the development and conduct of fire response drills on board vehicles carrying vessels.

items.title: Loss of bridge control: Human failure is normal - context is key
items.summary: When bridge control is lost in a functioning system, it can be easy to blame human error. But accidents rarely happen because of one mistake alone. Procedures, system design, fatigue, workload, communication and established ways of working can all set people up to fail. Understanding context is key

items.title: Hydrogen sulphide: The hidden danger outside enclosed spaces
items.summary: Hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) is well recognised as one of the most dangerous hazards associated with enclosed spaces on board ships. However, recent casualty investigations demonstrate that the greatest danger may arise before anyone enters the space.

items.title: Malaysia introduces new regulated sea areas
items.summary: Malaysia has introduced two new regulated sea areas near the eastern approaches to the Traffic Separation Scheme in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore. The regulations affect routing, anchoring, speed, cargo transfer and bunkering operations.

items.title: Cyber security controls for existing ships
items.summary: While mandatory cyber resilience requirements primarily apply to newbuilds, cyber threats affect ships regardless of age. IACS Recommendation No. 194 provides a practical baseline for strengthening cyber security controls across existing fleets.

items.title: Fish farm claims in China: lessons from a recent court judgement
items.summary: Fish farm contact incidents remain a recurring issue for vessels trading to Chinese coastal waters. Traditionally, such claims can be difficult for owners to defend, particularly where liability is argued from the mere fact that a vessel entered an aquaculture area. items.title: Loss of bridge control in functioning systems
items.summary: Effective control of a vessel can sometimes be lost even when equipment is working. In this article, we see how control settings applied by the crew can lead to serious accidents. items.title: Bearing failures: When normal readings hide the risk
items.summary: A serious engine-room incident shows how quickly a local bearing failure can escalate – even when standard temperature and pressure readings appear to be normal.

items.summary: A loss of bridge control, typically of steering, can have severe consequences for people, property and the environment. items.title: El Niño, Panama Canal restrictions, and routing off Cape Horn
items.summary: The Panama Canal remains the preferred route for vessels trading between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. items.title: AIS-assisted collisions: The risks of over-reliance
items.summary: AIS has evolved into an important safety aid for situational awareness and even collision avoidance. However, this evolution also brings new risks, and over-reliance on AIS may, in some cases, contribute to incidents rather than prevent them.
items.summary_zh: AIS雖然已成為重要的安全輔助工具，但過度依賴AIS可能在某些情況下導致事故，而非預防事故。

items.title: The US and China port fees: a comparison
items.summary: The US and China have introduced reciprocal port fees targeting vessels linked to each other’s countries, marking a novel use of port fees as geopolitical tools akin to tariffs. items.title: War in Ukraine – impact on the maritime situation
items.summary: The security situation in the Black Sea remains unstable, with commercial shipping facing an increased risk of attack. All transits and port calls should therefore be assessed individually, taking account of current threats, available guidance and appropriate mitigating measures.
